mainTopic: Worms in produce, in animals and in fish: when they count as forbidden שרצים. Then the list of creeping creatures, the לויתן, and the close of פרק אלו טרפות.
overview: The amud opens with the end of שמואל's ruling: produce that became wormy while still attached to the ground is forbidden as 'השרץ השורץ על הארץ'. The גמרא tries to support him from two ברייתות. It then rejects that proof: the ברייתות can be read as worms in the fruit (permitted) versus worms in the tree itself (forbidden). רב יוסף and רב אשי ask when a worm counts as having left its fruit, and both questions end in תיקו. The גמרא then discusses קוקיאני, worms found inside an animal's organs, and gives two versions of the ruling (in the name of רב ששת בריה דרב אידי, and in the second version רב שישא בריה דרב אידי) along with רב אשי's argument. The final הלכה is that קוקיאני are forbidden because worms crawl in through the snout. Worms in meat are forbidden, and worms in fish are permitted. רבינא explains this difference: an animal needs שחיטה, but fish are permitted just by being caught. The amud ends with a ברייתא listing the forbidden creeping creatures and a proof that the לויתן is a kosher fish, followed by the הדרן closing פרק אלו טרפות.

steps.title: שמואל's ruling: worms that grew while attached are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The end of שמואל's statement: produce that became wormy while still attached to the ground is forbidden because of the פסוק 'השרץ השורץ על הארץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A cucumber that became wormy] while attached to the ground is forbidden, because of the פסוק 'the creeping thing that creeps upon the earth'.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes שמואל's ruling, which began just before this section. A cucumber that became wormy while still growing on the ground is forbidden to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the cucumber is attached, it counts as part of the ground. So a worm that grew inside it counts as a creature that 'creeps upon the earth', and the Torah forbids those. A worm that grows in produce after it is picked does not fall under this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: While still attached to its plant or the ground (literally: 'in its stalk')
A creeping or swarming creature, forbidden to eat
'That creeps upon the earth': the words of the פסוק that define this prohibition
Forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the section is a test of this ruling: does a worm that grows in attached produce really count as 'on the earth'?

phrases.english: while attached to the ground, is forbidden
phrases.notes: This finishes שמואל's statement from just before: a cucumber that got wormy while still attached to the ground.

phrases.english: because of 'the creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאִבֶּיהָ אֲסוּרָה מִשּׁוּם ״הַשֶּׁרֶץ הַשֹּׁרֵץ עַל הָאָרֶץ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes שמואל's ruling, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Worms that develop in produce while it is attached to the ground are forbidden as שרץ השורץ על הארץ.

steps.title: Two ברייתות brought to support שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that two ברייתות support שמואל. One excludes worms found in lentils, beans, dates and figs. The other includes worms found in the roots of olive trees and vines.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? One ברייתא teaches: 'upon the earth' comes to exclude the זיזין in lentils, the gnats in beans, and the worms in dates and dried figs. Another ברייתא teaches: 'every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth' comes to include the worms in the roots of olives and the roots of vines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות that seem to point in opposite directions. It is setting up a proof for שמואל, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא uses the words 'upon the earth' to permit worms found in certain foods. The second uses the word 'every' to forbid worms found in the roots of trees and vines. Since one permits and one forbids, the גמרא will look for a difference between them that matches שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall we say this supports him?': the opening of a suggested proof
To exclude: these cases are left out of the prohibition
To include: these cases are added to the prohibition
A type of small insect found in lentils
A type of bean
Roots

phrases.english: Shall we say that this supports him?
For one ברייתא teaches: 'upon the earth' –
to exclude the zizin insects that are in lentils,
and the gnats that are in kelisim beans,
and the worm that is in dates and in dried figs.
And another ברייתא teaches:
'Every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth' –
phrases.notes: The extra word 'every' is what this ברייתא uses to add more cases.

phrases.english: to include the worm that is in the roots of olive trees
and that is in the roots of vines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for support for שמואל's ruling from ברייתות.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that worms in attached produce are forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות on the פסוק 'השרץ השורץ על הארץ': one excludes worms in lentils, beans, dates and figs, and the other includes worms in the roots of olives and vines.

steps.title: The proposed reading: attached is forbidden, detached is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that both ברייתות speak about fruit. The one that forbids is about attached fruit, and the one that permits is about detached fruit, exactly like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that both ברייתות speak about fruit, and this one is about fruit attached to the ground while that one is about fruit not attached?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the two ברייתות would prove שמואל right. The difference between them would be whether the fruit was still attached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both ברייתות are about worms in fruit, the only thing left to explain the different rulings is attachment. Attached fruit is forbidden and detached fruit is permitted, which is exactly what שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Isn't it that…?': introduces the suggested way to read a source
This one and that one: both sources
Fruit

phrases.english: Isn't it that both this one and that one are about fruit,
and this one is about fruit still attached,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the second ברייתא, which forbids.

phrases.english: and that one is about fruit not attached?
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the first ברייתא, which permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the two ברייתות in step 2.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contrast between the two ברייתות, read as attached versus detached fruit.

steps.title: Rejection: fruit versus the tree itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Both ברייתות may be about attached produce. Worms in the fruit are permitted, and worms in the tree itself are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Both are about produce that is attached, and there is no difficulty: this one is about worms in the fruit, and that one is about worms in the tree itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and offers a different way to explain the two ברייתות. In this reading, they give no support to שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of attached versus detached, the difference is where the worm is found: in the fruit or in the tree. If worms in attached fruit are permitted, that actually goes against שמואל. Only worms in the tree itself, like in its roots, count as 'on the earth'.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: the two sources can be reconciled
This one… that one: splitting two sources into two different cases
The tree itself

steps.confusionAlert: Watch how the dividing line moves. In the proof, both ברייתות were about fruit, split into attached and detached. In the rejection, both are about attached produce, split into fruit and tree. Under the rejection, worms in attached fruit are permitted, which goes against שמואל.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof for שמואל fails. The ברייתות can be read as fruit (permitted) versus tree (forbidden), with both attached, so they do not prove that attached fruit is forbidden.

phrases.english: No, both this one and that one are about produce that is attached,
and it is not difficult:
this one is about worms in the fruit,
that one is about worms in the tree itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 3 by giving a different way to divide the two ברייתות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof for שמואל from the ברייתות, without ruling directly on שמואל's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed both ברייתות speak about fruit. They can instead both speak about attached produce, split between fruit and tree, which takes away the support for שמואל and even goes against him.

steps.title: The wording of the ברייתא supports the new reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא's own words, 'the roots of olive trees and vines', fit the reading that it is talking about the tree itself, not the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording also proves this, because it says 'a worm in the roots of olive trees and in the roots of vines.' Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the answer from step 4 by pointing to the exact words of the second ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 the גמרא said that the forbidding ברייתא is about worms in the tree, not in the fruit. The ברייתא's wording proves this: it says 'roots', which is part of the tree, not fruit. So the attempt to use the two ברייתות as support for שמואל does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise. It shows that the text's exact words support this reading.
Roots, the base part of the tree.
Learn from it. This closes a proof.

steps.whatToRemember: Worms in the roots of a tree are forbidden, and worms inside the fruit are permitted. So these ברייתות do not prove שמואל's rule about fruit attached to the ground.

phrases.english: It is also precise,
phrases.notes: He means the exact words of the second ברייתא, the one that forbids.

phrases.english: as it teaches: 'A worm in the roots of olive trees
and in the roots of vines,'
learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 4 using the ברייתא's wording.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the forbidding ברייתא is about worms in the tree itself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's wording: 'עיקרי זיתים' and 'עיקרי גפנים'.

steps.title: When does a worm count as having left the fruit?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks three questions about a worm that grew inside fruit: what if it came out and died, what if only part came out, and what if it came out into the air. None are answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked: If it came out and died, what is the law? If part of it came out, what is the law? If it came out into the open air, what is the law? The question stays unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רב יוסף asks whether a worm that grew inside fruit becomes forbidden in certain borderline cases of leaving the fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A worm that grew inside detached fruit is permitted because it never 'swarmed on the earth'. רב יוסף asks how much leaving is needed to make it forbidden: coming out and dying right away, coming only partly out, or moving through the air without landing. The גמרא leaves all three questions open.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question, a real legal doubt that he wanted solved.
It separated, meaning the worm came out of the fruit.
What is the law?
The open air, outside the fruit.
Let it stand. The question stays without an answer.

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the worm is permitted or forbidden. It only means the גמרא could not decide the question.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef asked:
If it came out and died, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'It' is a worm that grew inside the fruit, and it died before it reached the ground.

phrases.english: If part of it came out, what is the law?
If it came out into the open air, what is the law?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new set of questions about what counts as 'swarming on the earth' for a worm that grew inside fruit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether dying right after leaving, leaving only partly, or leaving into the air is enough to count as 'swarming on the earth'.

steps.title: A worm moving on the date or into another date
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether a worm counts as having left its fruit if it crawls onto the top of the date, onto the top of its pit, or from one date into another. None are answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: If it moved onto the top of the date, what is the law? Onto the top of its pit, what is the law? From one date to another date, what is the law? The question stays unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues with more borderline questions, now from רב אשי, about a worm that moves around without really leaving the fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases are even closer to staying inside the fruit than רב יוסף's cases. The worm only moves to the outside of the same date, to its pit, or straight into another date. The question is whether this counts as 'swarming' or is just normal movement inside its food. Again the גמרא leaves it open.

keyTerms.meaning: The roof, meaning the top surface, of the date.
Its pit, the stone inside the date.
From one date to another date.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
If it moved onto the top of the date, what is the law?
Onto the top of its pit, what is the law?
From one date to another date, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means dates that touch each other, so the worm goes straight across without being in the open.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more borderline cases to רב יוסף's questions about when a worm counts as having left its fruit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether moving onto the date's surface, onto its pit, or into a touching date counts as 'swarming'.

steps.title: Worms inside an animal's organs are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי rules that קוקיאני, worms found inside an animal, are forbidden because they came in from the outside world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת the son of רב אידי said: קוקיאני are forbidden. Why? Because they came from the outside world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling: worms found inside an animal's body are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A worm that grows inside its food without leaving would be permitted. But these worms did not start inside the animal. They came from outside, so they already crawled on the ground and are forbidden as 'השרץ השורץ על הארץ'.

keyTerms.meaning: Worms found inside an animal's body, for example in the lung or liver.
They are forbidden.
They came from the outside world, so they were not created inside the animal.

steps.whatToRemember: The key question for any worm is where it came from. If it grew inside the food and never left, it can be permitted. If it came from outside, as with קוקיאני, it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet the son of Rav Idi said:
Kukeyanei are forbidden,
phrases.notes: These are worms found inside an animal's organs, like the lung or liver.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
They came from the outside world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from worms in fruit to worms found inside animals, using the same idea of where the worm came from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Worms found inside an animal's organs (קוקיאני) are forbidden, because they came from outside and already swarmed on the earth.

steps.title: רב אשי challenges the idea that the worms came from outside
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects to רב ששת's reason. If the worms came from the outside world, we would expect to find them in the digestive tract too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects to this: If they came from the outside world, they should be found in the digestive tract.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the reason given in step 8, that the worms came into the animal from outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that enters from outside normally goes in by mouth and passes through the intestines. Since these worms are found only in other organs and never in the digestive tract, רב אשי argues they must have grown inside the animal itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to, raises a strong challenge
From the outside world
The digestive tract or intestines

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objects to this:
If they came from the outside world,
they should be found in the digestive tract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's reason that קוקיאני came from outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Worms entering from outside would pass through the digestive tract, but they are not found there.

steps.title: Another version says the worms are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second version of the teaching, said in the name of רב שישא בריה דרב אידי. In this version, קוקיאני are permitted because they grow from the animal itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב שישא the son of רב אידי said: קוקיאני are permitted. What is the reason? They form from the animal itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the teaching, said here by רב שישא בריה דרב אידי. This version rules the opposite way: the worms are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the worms were forbidden because they came from outside. In this version, they are permitted because they grew from the animal's own body, so they count as part of the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Worms found inside an animal's organs
Are formed (literally, kneaded)
Permitted

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
Kukeyanei are permitted.
What is the reason? They form from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the ruling in step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קוקיאני are permitted because they grow from the animal itself.

steps.title: רב אשי calls the permission obvious
steps.stepSummary: In this second version, רב אשי agrees. He says it is obvious, because worms from outside would be found in the digestive tract.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is obvious, for if they came from the outside world, they would be found in the digestive tract!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי uses the same argument as in step 9, but here it supports the ruling instead of challenging it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of רב אשי's argument are the same in both versions. In the first version, they attack the ruling that the worms are forbidden. In the second version, they show the ruling that the worms are permitted is so clear it hardly needs to be said.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי says the same words in steps 9 and 11. Only their job changes: in step 9 they challenge the ruling, and in step 11 they support it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: It is obvious,
for if they came from the outside world,
they would be found in the digestive tract!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second version's ruling in step 10
steps.raayaSupportSource: Worms are not found in the digestive tract, so they did not come from outside.

steps.title: The final ruling: the worms are forbidden, but worms in fish are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that קוקיאני are forbidden, because worms crawl in through the sleeping animal's snout. Worms in meat are forbidden, and worms in fish are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: קוקיאני are forbidden. What is the reason? The animal sleeps, and worms enter it through its snout. Worms in meat are forbidden; worms in fish are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final הלכה and answers רב אשי's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי argued that the worms could not have come from outside, since they are not in the digestive tract. The answer is that they do come from outside, but through the nose, so they never pass through the intestines. The גמרא then adds a separate rule: worms in meat are forbidden and worms in fish are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: And the final הלכה is
Its snout or nose
Worms
Fish

steps.whatToRemember: קוקיאני are forbidden because worms enter through the snout. Worms in meat are forbidden, and worms in fish are permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling for worms found inside meat and fish.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: Kukeyanei are forbidden.
What is the reason?
The animal sleeps,
and worms enter it through its snout.
Worms of meat are forbidden;
those of fish are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two versions and answers רב אשי
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: קוקיאני are forbidden because worms enter through the snout. Worms in meat are forbidden, and worms in fish are permitted.

steps.title: רבינא eats fish with the worms hidden inside
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks his mother to hide the fish's worms inside it, and he will eat the fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to his mother: Hide them inside for me, and I will eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing רבינא acting on the rule that worms in fish are permitted. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא is willing to eat the worms, since they are permitted. He just does not want to see them.

keyTerms.meaning: Hide inside, bury within

phrases.english: Ravina said to his mother:
Hide them inside for me, and I will eat.
phrases.notes: He means the worms in the fish. He doesn't want to see them while he eats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the fish rule from step 12 being put into practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Worms in fish may be eaten.

steps.title: רב משרשיא challenges רבינא from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא asks רבינא how this differs from a ברייתא that uses a פסוק to forbid worms in animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא the son of רב אחא said to רבינא: What is different from that which is taught: "And their carcasses you shall detest," to include the worms in an animal?
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא challenges רבינא's practice using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from a פסוק that worms in an animal are forbidden. The question is why worms in fish should be any different. The next step gives רבינא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
To include
You shall detest (treat as forbidden)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya son of Rav Acha said to Ravina:
What is different from that which is taught:
"And their carcasses you shall detest,"
to include the worms in an animal?

steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's eating of worms in fish
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא uses a פסוק to forbid worms in animals, so why would worms in fish be permitted?

steps.title: Animals need slaughter, fish do not
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that worms in an animal stay forbidden because שחיטה cannot permit them. Fish need no שחיטה at all, so worms forming inside a fish begin in a permitted state.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: How can you compare them? An animal becomes permitted only through שחיטה. These worms are not helped by the שחיטה, so they stay forbidden. But fish become permitted just by being gathered up, so when these worms form inside them, they form already permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers רב משרשיא's question from step 14. He shows that the ברייתא about worms in animals does not apply to fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before an animal is slaughtered, everything in it is forbidden, and only שחיטה makes it permitted. The worms gain nothing from the שחיטה, so they stay forbidden. Fish never need שחיטה, so nothing inside them ever started out forbidden, and worms that grow inside them are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: "How can you compare?" Used to reject a comparison.
Kosher slaughter, which makes an animal permitted to eat.
Gathering. Simply catching fish, with no slaughter needed.
They form, or take shape (the worms developing inside).
In a permitted state.

steps.whatToRemember: Worms in meat are forbidden because שחיטה does not permit them. Worms in fish are permitted because fish are permitted without שחיטה, so the worms start out permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying worms in fish are a different kind of creature. The difference is about how the host becomes permitted: an animal needs שחיטה, and a fish only needs to be caught.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the practical rule from step 12: worms found inside fish may be eaten along with the fish.

phrases.english: He said to him: How can these be compared?
phrases.notes: רבינא is answering רב משרשיא's question from the last step.

phrases.english: An animal becomes permitted only through slaughter,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי מִדְּלָא קָא מַהְנְיָא לְהוּ שְׁחִיטָה –
phrases.english: and these worms, since slaughter does not work for them,
remain in their forbidden state.
But fish are permitted by merely gathering them,
so when these worms form,
they form in a permitted state.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב משרשיא's challenge from step 14 by showing the ברייתא about animals does not apply to fish.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק) between how animals and fish become permitted.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since worms in animals are forbidden by a פסוק, worms in fish should be forbidden too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Animals need שחיטה, which does nothing for the worms. Fish need only gathering, so their worms form already permitted.

steps.title: Which creeping creatures the פסוק forbids
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains each phrase of ויקרא 11:42. One phrase names a main creature (snake, scorpion, centipede), and the extra word next to it adds similar creatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "goes on its belly" means the snake. "Whatever" adds the earthworm and creatures like it. "On all fours" means the scorpion. "Whatever goes" adds the beetle and creatures like it. "Many feet" means the centipede. "Or whatever" adds creatures like it, and creatures like those.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא on the creeping creatures forbidden in ויקרא 11:42. It stays with the general theme of forbidden שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase in the פסוק names one main creature. The extra word ("whatever," "whatever goes," "or whatever") is read as a ריבוי that adds similar creatures. The last ריבוי reaches even further, to creatures similar to the similar ones.

keyTerms.meaning: Belly. Creatures that crawl on their bellies.
To include. An extra word teaches that more cases are covered.
Earthworm.
Beetle.
Centipede.
What is similar to the similar. A second level of including.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Goes upon the belly": this is the snake,
"Whatever": to include the earthworm
and what is similar to the earthworm,
"Upon all fours": this is the scorpion,
"Whatever goes": to include the beetle
and what is similar to the beetle,
"Has many feet": this is the centipede,
"Or whatever": to include what is similar
and what is similar to the similar.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוֹלֵךְ עַל גָּחוֹן זֶה נָחָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the worm discussion to a ברייתא explaining the list of forbidden creeping creatures in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The snake, scorpion and centipede are forbidden, along with every creature similar to them, and even creatures similar to those.

steps.title: The לויתן is a kosher fish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן דורמסקית proves from פסוקים in איוב that the לויתן has scales and fins, so it is a kosher fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן דורמסקית says: the לויתן is a kosher fish. It says, "His pride is his armor" and "Under him are sharp potsherds." "His armor" means his scales. "Sharp potsherds under him" means the fins he swims with.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא about kashrus. It proves that the famous לויתן is a kosher fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fish is kosher if it has scales and fins. רבי יוסי reads the "armor" in איוב as the לויתן's scales and the "sharp potsherds" under it as its fins. Having both signs makes it a kosher fish.

keyTerms.meaning: The giant sea creature described in איוב.
A kosher fish.
Shields. Here, armor.
Scales.
Fins.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹרְמַסְקִית אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yosei ben Durmaskit says:
The leviathan is a kosher fish,
as it is said: "His armor is his pride,"
and "Sharpest potsherds are under him."
"His armor": these are his scales,
"Sharpest potsherds are under him":
these are the fins with which he swims.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹרְמַסְקִית אוֹמֵר: לִוְיָתָן דָּג טָהוֹר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא on kosher and non-kosher creatures, this time about fish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לויתן is a kosher fish, because the פסוקים show it has scales and fins.

steps.title: Hadran: Closing the פרק אלו טרפות
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the פרק אלו טרפות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק אלו טרפות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the פרק of אלו טרפות with the traditional closing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן marks the end of the פרק and expresses our hope to come back and learn it again. It adds no new הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The closing line said when finishing a פרק.
The name of this פרק, about the injuries that make an animal טרפה.

steps.whatToRemember: The פרק אלו טרפות is now complete.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "Eilu Tereifos."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the last ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The end of the פרק אלו טרפות.
